rites.name: Ceranum
rites.text: Ceranum is the concept of resonance held in the Singing, the undated sounding in which the first roots of Eliolerae condense out of silence. It is less a thing than a pitch that other things must match to become real. Its earliest act was to bind loose matter into the first lasting shapes.

rites.name: Lisor
rites.text: A brief chant sung by two companions in a rowdy tale, said to teach the basics of blundering, foolish speech to any listener who joins in.

rites.name: Syethasha
rites.text: Syethasha is the concept of threshold-keeping in Eliolerae, the principle by which a door holds one world apart from the next. In the Courts of the second Era it is invoked whenever a new passage between worlds is sealed or opened. Its presence is felt as a quiet pressure rather than as any visible form.

rites.name: Karuthok
rites.text: Karuthok is the concept of a binding oath, the invisible thread that holds a sworn word to its speaker across the Courts of Eliolerae. Its power is felt most in the Age of Sundering, when landfall snapped old oaths and the councils had to forge new doors between worlds to restore what was broken.

rites.name: Thurden
rites.text: Thurden is the concept of a binding oath, personified as the quiet clerk who records every promise made in the Courts of Eliolerae. During the Age of Sundering, Thurden's ledger became the only thing holding the new doors between worlds in place when landfall broke the old bonds.

rites.name: Tolares
rites.text: A solitary voice rises in a chant offered without instruments. It is performed by a single singer within a larger cycle of verses.

rites.name: Ameontus
rites.text: A brief chant performed by a singer named Ruvel to his beloved, recalled in a memory scene during a later tale of the realm.

rites.name: Xaithess
rites.text: Xaithess is a concept of Eliolerae, a binding principle that the makers set into the Weave during the Seeding, when quiet powers were laid to sleep beneath the world. Across the Age of Sundering it persisted as the thread that held broken oaths together when landfall split old alliances apart.

rites.name: Ilyanneth
rites.text: Ilyanneth is a concept of the Arcane Realm in Eliolerae, a notion of the Weave as it was planted during the Seeding, when quiet powers slept beneath the surface of the world. Its meaning shifted in the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between those who held the Weave together.

rites.name: Orentes
rites.text: A short chant sung by a figure named Dareth to urge a band of companions named Jorvel and his crew to remain loyal to one another.

rites.name: Tenrakaleno
rites.text: Tenrakaleno is a concept of the Arcane Realm in Eliolerae, a principle of rooted growth that the first sovereign bound into the groves during the Sundering. It is said to hold the Pact's oaths in the living wood, so that a broken branch remembers the word it was sworn upon.

rites.name: Corirnialum
rites.text: Corirnialum is the concept of a living lattice of light that ran through the worlds of Eliolerae before the Sundering, binding their oaths into a single song. When the Fall split the realms into Shards, it became the thread the sworn orders still follow in the Holy Age, kept alive in temple flame.

rites.name: Khuggurn
rites.text: Khuggurn is a concept of Eliolerae, a binding principle of the Arcane Realm that the orders of the Holy Age claimed to have shaped from the wreckage of the Sundering. It is said to be the will that held the Shards to the Pact, and its temples still burn with a flame that does not consume.

rites.name: Miemiorliel
rites.text: Miemiorliel is the concept of walls and thresholds in Eliolerae, the notion that a boundary holds its shape even as the things beyond it change. During the Walled Age it was embodied in the orders that raised and guarded the first crossings, where its quiet persistence was felt more than seen. Its power is steady and enduring rather than explosive.

rites.name: Noleostia
rites.text: Noleostia is the concept of a sealed wall-line in Eliolerae, a boundary of stone and standing vow that the orders of the Walled Age maintained for centuries. It is remembered in the churches as the first thing that held back the crossings. Its power lay less in force than in the refusal to give ground.

rites.name: Montia
rites.text: A bandaging healer chants an improvised verse over a patient's pulse. The chant is a sung performance tied to a larger tale about the mind.

rites.name: Vonasus
rites.text: A distant guiding art that lets a practitioner influence a far-off mechanism through a shared link. It is practiced as a playful contest of skill in a networked arena.

rites.name: Alaarae
rites.text: Alaarae is a sealed ritual-event in Eliolerae where a circle of hungry novices bind a stolen trinket to a fourth willing soul, sending a surge of borrowed will through the realm's Arcane veil. Those who witness it describe the sudden sensation of their own fears being answered by something eager to please.

rites.name: Siluarlae
rites.text: Siluarlae is an arcane event in the sixth age of Eliolerae, a sealing rite where a cloud of silver lattice-light is drawn down across a sleeping river-valley to bind its restless undercurrent. The event is remembered as the moment the valley's spirits chose stillness over the world's ruin.

rites.name: Nuilaerae
rites.text: Nuilaerae is a fading hymn-spirit of the Arcane realm, said to be the last note of a choir that sang the first dawn into being. Its voice still reshapes the faintest threads of fate, though its brightness dims with each age of quiet. Scholars of Eliolerae debate whether it remembers the stars it once tuned or merely echoes them.

rites.name: Feneste
rites.text: Feneste is the concept of the threshold where a single choice splits into branching futures, and it is shelved in the Library's quiet archive of outcomes. In the Age of the first sovereign, groves and growing kingdoms take their shape from its quiet pressure, though it rarely acts directly.
